paper-ganblr-interpretable-tabular-2023.summary: Proposes GANBLR, which replaces the neural generator of a tabular GAN with a Bayesian-network classifier so that the generative model exposes explicit feature interactions and per-feature importance, making both the generated data and the generation process interpretable while matching neural models on machine-learning utility. CTGAN is the state-of-the-art benchmark the paper measures itself against, and its mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling are set out at length as the design GANBLR departs from.

paper-paacda-comprehensive-corruption-de.summary: This paper proposes PAACDA (Proximity based Adamic Adar Corruption Detection Algorithm), an unsupervised method for detecting corrupted data in datasets, distinguishing corruption detection from standard outlier detection and benchmarking against methods like K-means, Isolation Forest, and LOF. The paper briefly notes that GANs could be a plausible approach for regenerating corrupted data, citing CTGAN alongside another reference in passing, without implementing or evaluating it.

paper-tool-dataset-paper-realistic-2023.summary: This paper introduces ConGRASS, a web-based tool that trains a conditional tabular GAN on a real Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) dataset to generate arbitrarily large, realistic synthetic ABAC datasets for reproducible access-control research. The authors explicitly use the CTGAN library from the SDV ecosystem as their generative model, and evaluate outputs using the SDV/SDMetrics CSTest score and the Table Evaluator tool associated with SDV. CTGAN, run as the core generator of the entire pipeline, is the load-bearing component of the whole empirical study.

paper-trend-aware-imputation-generative-.summary: This paper proposes TrendGAN, a GAN-based imputation method for time series that uses a de-noising auto-encoder for end-to-end training and a bidirectional GRU generator/discriminator to capture temporal trends, evaluated on four real datasets against baseline imputation methods. The abstract does not describe TGAN being run or compared as a baseline. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) appears only in the citation list as related prior GAN-based generative work.

paper-electra-predicate-aware-aqp-2022.summary: Proposes ELECTRA, an approximate query processing method that learns a conditional generative model over a database so that a query with several predicates can be answered from generated samples rather than from a stored uniform sample, which is where sampling-based AQP loses accuracy on selective queries. CTGAN is one of the generative baselines run for comparison, taken from the sdv-dev repository, and the paper's motivating limitation is CTGAN's support for only a single generation condition, which forces the authors to pick one predicate at random when using it.

paper-twin-driven-cyber-physical-2022.summary: This paper proposes 'Data Twin,' a machine-learning-based approach to simplify high-fidelity Digital Twin virtual models, and a supporting microservice architecture called Cyber-Physical Factory (CPF) with Physical and Cyber War Rooms for simulating aerospace composite-material manufacturing shop floors. It targets Industry 4.0 adoption in aircraft manufacturing where building detailed physical simulation models is costly. TGAN is only mentioned in passing among open-source data synthesis tools (synthpop, simPop, TGAN) in a list, with no evidence it was run.

paper-deep-feature-synthesis-accurate-20.summary: A short conference paper applying Deep Feature Synthesis and Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CTGAN) to the Breast Cancer Coimbra dataset, testing whether synthetic augmentation improves classifier performance (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, Naive Bayes, kNN). The authors train models on CTGAN-generated data and test on the original data, finding that CTGAN output degrades performance and fails to reproduce the intrinsic feature correlations of the medical data. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional GAN for tabular data, is run directly as the synthetic data generator whose output is evaluated (and ultimately rejected) across the paper's experiments.

paper-federated-tabular-risk-2022.summary: Examines whether federated learning over tabular data leaks training records, treating tabular GANs as the class of model under attack. CTGAN is cited as a member of that class rather than run.

paper-genethos-synthetic-generation-syst.summary: This paper presents GenEthos, an interactive GUI tool for synthetic tabular data generation that incorporates bias detection (via metrics like SPD and DI) and bias mitigation algorithms (e.g., Learning Fair Representation) for datasets such as German Credit and Adult. It evaluates several mitigation techniques and reports that LFR substantially reduces statistical parity difference on original data, concluding that fairness must be actively checked in both real and synthetic data. In its related-work review the authors describe CTGAN's architecture in detail -- its mode-specific normalization, conditional vector, and training-by-sampling design -- and separately cite the TGAN paper, but neither model is shown to be run within their own tool.

paper-generation-synthetic-full-scale-20.summary: This engineering paper addresses the scarcity of full-scale burst test data for corroded pipelines by generating synthetic test records using a tabular generative adversarial network approach. The synthetic data is intended to augment limited experimental datasets for pipeline failure-pressure modeling. The work cites the TGAN (2018) paper as the basis for its tabular GAN method, though it is unclear from available evidence whether the sdv-dev TGAN package was run directly or reimplemented.

paper-generating-artificial-scalability-.summary: This thesis proposes a method for generating artificial Twitter data — using analytical modeling, tf-idf and bag-of-words — to test the scalability and accuracy of a followee recommender system without relying on hard-to-obtain real social data. A simulator is built to exercise the recommender under a distributed environment using this synthetic tweet data. The Synthetic Data Vault is mentioned only in passing as related work on generative modeling of relational databases, not used in the thesis's own method.

paper-holdout-empirical-assessment-mixed.summary: This paper introduces a holdout-based empirical framework for assessing the fidelity and privacy risk of mixed-type tabular synthetic data, using statistical distances between lower-dimensional marginals for fidelity and distance-to-closest-record for privacy. The framework is demonstrated across seven synthetic data solutions and four datasets, comparing AI-based generators against traditional perturbation techniques. Four of the seven evaluated generators -- CopulaGAN, CTGAN, Gaussian Copula, and TVAE -- are drawn from MIT's Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library and run as evaluation subjects within this benchmark.

paper-gain-pseudo-label-conditional-2021.summary: This paper proposes PC-GAIN, an unsupervised missing-data imputation method that extends the GAIN framework by pre-training on low-missing-rate data to synthesize pseudo-labels, then using an auxiliary classifier within the generative adversarial framework to improve imputation quality over GAIN and other baselines. The paper is about imputation for incomplete tabular data, not synthetic data generation per se. TGAN is cited only in passing as prior work describing a tabular GAN with a recurrent generator architecture, with no experiments run using it.

paper-privacy-sensitive-business-models-.summary: This paper reviews the literature on organizational barriers to adopting privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) in data-driven business models, using the TOE (Technology-Organization-Environment) framework to explain why firms resist PET adoption despite calls from research streams to use them. It identifies unclear economic impact and lack of relative advantage as the main adoption barriers. SDV's original synthetic data paper is cited once in passing as an example of synthetic data protecting the nature of underlying data.

paper-gsp-auction-mechanism-ranking-2019.summary: This paper proposes a generalized second-price (GSP) auction mechanism for ranking and prioritizing Bitcoin transactions within blockchain mining pools, addressing incentive design in transaction fee markets. It is published in Decision Support Systems and its empirical/theoretical focus is on blockchain economics rather than data synthesis. The metadata indicates it cites the original SDV DSAA-2016 paper, but no citing sentence, abstract, or full text is available to establish how or why SDV is referenced.

paper-morpher-platform-support-modeling-.summary: This paper presents MORPHER, a hybrid cloud/on-premise platform designed to support research clinicians in developing and externally validating clinical prediction models (CPMs) for outcomes such as Acute Kidney Injury, addressing gaps in existing rapid-prototyping tools for the clinical ML domain. To illustrate the platform's validation step, the authors generated 25 synthetic datasets. TGAN, the GAN-based tabular data synthesizer from the SDV family, is run as the generator producing these illustrative synthetic validation datasets.

paper-tabular-disentanglement-framework-.summary: Sets out a formal framework for tabular data disentanglement, defining the extraction and extrapolation queries a data owner issues, the external knowledge available, and the utility and privacy objectives against which a latent representation is scored, so that otherwise unrelated approaches can be read as instances of one flow. CTGAN and TVAE are named as two of the existing approaches the framework subsumes, cited for conditional generation under specified conditions and for latent-representation learning respectively, with mode collapse and generation quality given as their limitations; neither is run.

paper-rsdv-preprint-2026.summary: Argues that R has had good pieces of the synthesis workflow but no native version of the copula-based joint model that SDV popularised, and introduces `rsdv` to close that gap: a Gaussian copula fitted jointly over numerical, categorical and boolean columns, with conditional sampling, declarative row-level constraints, and three reports. Benchmarked against synthpop and arf on UCI Adult, synthpop wins on marginal fidelity while rsdv matches it on privacy. This is a port of SDV's design into another language rather than a use of it — the metadata system, the constraint-by-rejection-sampling mechanism and the quality/validity/privacy reports are modelled directly on SDV and SDMetrics, and the package calls itself "the R Synthetic Data Vault".

preprint-tide-customisable-dataset-gener.summary: This paper presents Tide, an open-source, customisable generator that produces graph-based synthetic financial transaction networks incorporating structural and temporal money-laundering patterns, releasing two reference datasets and benchmarking detection models (LightGBM, XGBoost, etc.) on them. It positions Tide against prior tabular/graph synthetic generators, noting related-work architectures such as GAN-based tabular approaches and a Gaussian-copula method (SynthAML) as limited in capturing network topology and temporal dynamics. CTGAN is cited only in a related-work sentence as a GAN architecture that has shown success reproducing tabular and time-series distributions, without being run or benchmarked in the study.

preprint-explainable-model-detecting-mal.summary: This preprint proposes a machine-learning pipeline for detecting malicious Ethereum smart contracts from EVM opcode frequency features, using SMOTE to balance the dataset, entropy-based binning to binarize features, and LIME to explain the classifier's predictions, achieving 99% detection with a 0.01 false positive rate. In the introduction the authors mention a future direction of synthetically generating malicious contracts using a conditional GAN to train an adversarial-resistant classifier, citing the CTGAN paper, but no such generation is implemented or run in the reported experiments (SMOTE is used instead). CTGAN is cited only bibliographically as inspiration for a proposed but unexecuted future extension.

paper-debt-collection-negotiation-llm-20.summary: Builds an evaluation system for debt collection negotiation that scores an agent on both the negotiation process and its outcome, and proposes a multi-agent framework with planning and judging modules tuned by direct preference optimization with reject sampling. CTGAN produces the benchmark itself: the 975-record debt dataset is synthesized from real records held by a financial technology company in order to meet privacy compliance, then sampled to match the original distribution by gender, overdue days and loan amount, so every result in the paper is measured on CTGAN output.

preprint-automated-privacy-preserving-te.summary: This paper proposes AUTOPRIV, a meta-learning framework that automates privacy-preserving data configuration by predicting the predictive performance and privacy risk of a large set of privacy-preservation techniques, removing the need for manual expert tuning. It evaluates six synthesis/protection methods, including deep-learning generators, differentially-private GANs, and an interpolation-based approach, across multiple hyperparameter optimisation strategies. SDV's CopulaGAN, TVAE, and CTGAN are run directly from the SDV library as three of the six generation methods whose predictive performance and privacy risk are evaluated and compared.

preprint-evaluating-utility-synthetic-ba.summary: This preprint develops an evaluation framework for the utility and privacy of synthetic banking microdata, applying it to financial usage indices, term deposit yield curves, and credit card transition matrices using confidential data from the Central Bank of Paraguay. The empirical comparison runs several differentially private synthesizers (MST, AIM, PAC, DPCTGAN, PATECTGAN), finding marginal-based inference methods generally outperform GAN-based ones for these applications. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited and its mode-specific normalization, data imbalance handling, and training-by-sampling techniques are described in prose as the basis for the DP-adapted CTGAN variants actually evaluated, rather than being run itself.

preprint-predicting-reliability-image-cl.summary: The paper proposes a Gaussian-process-based oversampling method (GPS-SMOTE) to rebalance a highly imbalanced training set used to train a 'distortion-classifier' that predicts whether an image classifier remains reliable under a given distortion level. It benchmarks against numerous imbalance-handling baselines, including cost-sensitive learning, under/over-sampling methods, ensemble methods, and generative models. CTGAN and TVAE, taken from the sdv-dev/CTGAN GitHub repository, are run unmodified as generative-model baselines for oversampling the minority class and are outperformed by the proposed method.

paper-structured-evaluation-synthetic-20.summary: Argues that synthetic-data evaluation is a scattered collection of metrics with no account of what each one is sensitive to, and builds a structured framework that separates a synthesizer's ability to model the data-generating process from its ability to reproduce the sample, testing the framework by evaluating eight synthesizers on three datasets. Four of those eight come from SDV — GaussianCopula, CopulaGAN, CTGAN and TVAE — with the copula-based and autoencoder-based entries attributed to Patki et al. and the GAN and VAE entries to Xu et al.

preprint-embeddings-tabular-survey-2023.summary: A survey paper that surveys methods for learning embeddings/latent representations of tabular data, splitting the field into a classical learning phase (SVMs, regression, tree-based methods) and a modern machine learning phase using deep learning approaches, and cataloguing tasks and datasets used in the literature. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) is cited only in the reference list as prior work on synthesizing tabular data via GANs, in a passing citation about causes of low-quality tabular data such as class imbalance and outliers, with no engagement or experiments involving it.

preprint-isoex-explainable-unsupervised-.summary: IsoEx is a feature-based unsupervised anomaly detection method for identifying malicious command lines in cybersecurity SOC/CERT log investigations, combining structural log features with SHAP-based explainability. To address rare/imbalanced binary features in their dataset, the authors trialed several synthetic data generation techniques and settled on CopulaGAN as the best trade-off between data coherence and computation time. SDV's CopulaGAN synthesizer is run directly to generate synthetic data augmenting rare features prior to SHAP analysis.

paper-domias-membership-inference-2023.summary: Reframes membership inference against synthetic data as overfitting detection: DOMIAS scores a target record by the ratio of its density under the synthetic distribution to its density under a reference population, so that records the generator has locally overfitted are identified without assuming the attacker knows the training procedure. TVAE, released with CTGAN, is the generator the attack is developed and calibrated against — training-set size and epoch count are swept on TVAE to control how much it overfits, the private heart-failure experiment generates from TVAE, and CTGAN and TVAE both appear in the wider comparison of generators by privacy-utility trade-off.

preprint-assessing-deep-generative-model.summary: This preprint evaluates three recent GAN architectures for generating synthetic network load (time-series telecom traffic) data, testing whether models trained on the synthetic data can substitute for real data in downstream forecasting tasks, using the Telecom Italia dataset and a mix of qualitative and quantitative metrics. CTGAN is cited as one of the SDV-family papers referenced for one of the three evaluated GAN architectures. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization approach is one of the generative methods run as an evaluation subject alongside the other GAN architectures compared.

paper-g2a2-graph-generator-2022.summary: Addresses the shortage of dynamic attributed graph datasets carrying anomaly ground truth by generating them: a temporal bipartite graph is produced first, anomalies are injected to emulate burstiness and propagation, and node attributes are then synthesised and mapped onto the graph. CTGAN performs that last stage, run as two separate instances trained on the normal and anomalous partitions of a source table so that the attributes attached to injected anomalies come from the anomalous distribution.

preprint-sequential-models-synthetic-vau.summary: This paper introduces the Sequential SDV framework and its novel conditional probabilistic auto-regressive (CPAR) model for generating multi-sequence synthetic data, along with a new evaluation metric (Multi-Sequence Aggregate Similarity) to compare sequential and non-sequential synthetic data quality. Authored by the DataCebo/MIT DAI Lab team behind SDV, it positions the new sequential model within the broader open-source SDV library alongside existing models such as the multi-table SDV model and CTGAN. CTGAN is run as a non-sequential baseline against which the new CPAR model's synthetic data quality is compared, and a Gaussian Copula model from SDV is applied to a context table in the pipeline.

preprint-synthesis-adversarial-ddos-atta.summary: This preprint studies how GAN-synthesized DDoS traffic can be used as adversarial examples to probe and expose weaknesses in machine-learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS). The authors generate tabular attack data with a GAN-based approach, converting categorical fields via one-hot encoding with noise, and evaluate the impact of these synthesized adversarial attacks on IDS detection performance. The paper cites the TGAN work (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) specifically for its categorical one-hot-encoding-with-noise technique, adopting the idea in prose rather than running the SDV-family TGAN implementation itself.

preprint-analysis-deployment-models-trai.summary: This paper studies how differentially private synthetic tabular data generation affects both model utility and algorithmic fairness, and shows that model performance evaluated on synthetic data can misestimate real-world deployment performance. The authors run three DP synthesizers (PrivBayes, QUAIL+PATECTGAN, QUAIL+DPCTGAN) on the Adult and COMPAS datasets and measure utility/fairness gaps between evaluation and deployment. CTGAN, as introduced by Xu et al. (2019), underlies two of the three synthesizers evaluated, combined with PATE and DP-SGD mechanisms as the conditional generator producing the differentially private synthetic training data.

preprint-generating-annotated-training-o.summary: This preprint proposes a proof-of-concept method for autonomously generating annotated training data for 6D object pose estimation in robotic grasping, aiming to reduce reliance on expensive expert-annotated or simulation-based datasets and to close the sim-to-real domain gap. The approach is evaluated in two grasping experiments against a non-autonomously generated dataset. The work cites the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) paper, apparently in passing as related prior art on synthetic/automated data generation, with no indication it is run or adapted.

preprint-adversarially-learned-inference.summary: This paper proposes an adversarially-trained ensemble of discrete undirected graphical models (AGMs) that generalizes across inference tasks without retraining, evaluated on MNIST and Caltech-101 for both generation and inference quality. The CTGAN paper (Xu et al. 2019) appears only in the reference list, with no engagement in the body text describing use of CTGAN's methods or model. CTGAN is cited only, never run or discussed in the body.

preprint-establishing-fair-care-efficien.summary: This preprint examines the ethical, legal, and infrastructural considerations for generating and sharing synthetic health data in Canada, proposing a framework that balances the social benefits of data-driven innovation against the privacy risks of data sharing. It advocates for FAIR- and CARE-aligned synthetic data infrastructure and touches on federated learning as a complementary privacy-preserving approach. CTGAN is cited as a source of synthetic data generation methodology relevant to this landscape but is not itself run or evaluated in the work.

It discusses design choices around noise structure, collinearity, class distributions, and feature complexity, and provides visualization tools for exploratory analysis and teaching.
